issues.legal_issue: A contractor’s notice of its proposed rate for additional work, followed by the engineer’s failure to cancel the order, does not by itself establish agreement to that rate.
material_facts: The contract provided a procedure for additional or altered work for which no rate was specified or agreed: the contractor could notify the engineer of its proposed rate, and the engineer could cancel the order if it did not agree.
The contractor notified the engineer of its proposed rate and carried out the additional work, but the engineer did not positively agree to that rate.
The contractor claimed payment for the additional work at the rate in its notice.
issues.conclusion: The contractor was not entitled to payment at the rate it had proposed merely because the engineer did not cancel the order. The claims for the additional work at that rate were rejected; where the contractor proceeded without an agreed rate, payment was governed by the contract’s rate-fixing procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Under clause 14, failure to cancel an order after receiving the contractor’s proposed rate does not amount to acceptance of that rate; agreement requires a positive act by the engineer. Where the contractor commences work or incurs expenditure before rates are determined, the contract provides for payment at the rate fixed by the Engineer-in-charge, with a rate dispute referred to the Superintending Engineer. The court rejected the High Court’s interpretation of clause 14.

rule.if: contractual_extra_work_claim and additional_work_ordered and no_applicable_rate_or_agreed_rate and contractor_notified_proposed_rate and engineer_did_not_positively_accept_rate

predicates.contractual_extra_work_claim: The proceeding includes a contractor’s claim for payment for additional or altered work under a contract.
predicates.additional_work_ordered: The employer’s engineer directed the contractor to carry out additional or altered work.
predicates.no_applicable_rate_or_agreed_rate: No rate in the contract’s applicable schedule or agreed rate covered the additional or altered work.
predicates.contractor_notified_proposed_rate: The contractor informed the engineer of the rate it intended to charge for the work.
predicates.engineer_did_not_positively_accept_rate: The engineer did not take a positive step agreeing to the contractor’s proposed rate.

issues.definition: When a contractor claims payment for ordered additional work with no applicable or agreed rate, notice of a proposed rate and the engineer’s failure to cancel the order do not make that rate an agreed rate if the engineer did not positively accept it.

issues.legal_issue: A contractual exclusion of compensation for curtailed work does not bar a claim where a change in specifications increases the work and does not curtail it.
material_facts: The contract allowed changes to specifications and excluded compensation for specified stoppages, reductions, or alterations involving curtailment of work.
The employer changed the specification for slab work, requiring more reinforcement and increasing the contractor’s cost rather than reducing or curtailing the work.
The contractor sought compensation for the additional cost caused by the changed specification.
issues.conclusion: The contractual exclusion for curtailment did not apply, and the contractor’s claim for the additional cost was well founded.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 15 excluded compensation for stoppage or reduction of work and for alterations involving curtailment. It did not apply to a change that involved no curtailment and instead increased the work and its cost.

rule.if: contractual_alteration_compensation_claim and specification_was_changed and change_increased_work_or_cost and work_was_not_curtailed

predicates.contractual_alteration_compensation_clai: The proceeding includes a contractor’s claim for compensation arising from a change to the contracted work.
predicates.specification_was_changed: The employer altered a specification governing the contractor’s work.
predicates.change_increased_work_or_cost: The altered specification required additional work or increased the contractor’s cost.
predicates.work_was_not_curtailed: The change did not reduce or curtail the work originally contemplated.

issues.definition: If a specification change increases work or cost without curtailing the work, the contractual exclusion for curtailment does not bar the contractor’s compensation claim.

issues.legal_issue: A contractually required written notice before transferring work to another contractor is mandatory, and a contractor may recover damages when the work is transferred without that notice.
material_facts: The contract required the engineer to give the contractor written notice before stopping the work and having it carried out by another contractor.
The employer had represented that it would entrust the contractor with the work, but instead arranged for another contractor to do it without giving the required written notice.
The contractor claimed compensation for the work transferred to the other contractor.
issues.conclusion: The written-notice condition was mandatory, and the contractor was entitled to damages because the work was transferred without the required notice.
issues.legal_principle: Clause 15 expressly required written notice before the engineer stopped work and arranged for another contractor to perform it. The court held that compliance with this condition was mandatory.

rule.if: contractual_claim_for_transferred_work and employer_assigned_work_to_another_contractor and contract_required_prior_written_notice and prior_written_notice_was_not_given

predicates.contractual_claim_for_transferred_work: The proceeding includes a contractor’s claim for compensation for work taken from it and assigned elsewhere.
predicates.employer_assigned_work_to_another_contra: The employer arranged for another contractor to perform work that had been contemplated for the claimant contractor.
predicates.contract_required_prior_written_notice: The contract required written notice before the work could be stopped and assigned to another contractor.
predicates.prior_written_notice_was_not_given: The employer did not give the contractor the required written notice before transferring the work.

issues.definition: When a contract requires prior written notice before work is transferred, transferring the work without that notice entitles the contractor to damages.

issues.legal_issue: A special limitation period for acts done or purportedly done in pursuance of a statutory enactment does not govern a contractual claim for non-payment based on breach when the non-payment has no reasonable connection with a statutory duty.
material_facts: A statutory housing body was responsible for carrying out housing schemes and entered into, or was deemed to have entered into, a construction contract for that purpose.
The contractor’s suit sought money allegedly due as damages or compensation for breach of the contract, including non-payment of amounts claimed.
The alleged non-payment was not shown to have a reasonable connection with a duty imposed on the statutory body or its agents by the enactment.
issues.conclusion: The contractual claim for non-payment was not an act done or purportedly done in pursuance of the enactment, so the special six-month limitation period did not bar the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 64 of the Bombay Housing Board Act, 1948 applied to suits concerning things done or purportedly done in pursuance of the Act. Although sections 19 and 23 and section 24(f) concerned the Board’s statutory housing functions, a claim for non-payment arising from breach of contract was distinct from performance of those functions and lacked a reasonable connection to a statutory duty. The court followed The Trustees of Port of Bombay v. The Premier Automobiles Ltd., approved The Municipal Borough of Ahmedabad v. Jayantilal Chhotalal Patel, and discussed Athimannil Muhammad v. The Malabar District Board and Jalgaon Borough Municipality v. The Khandesh Spinning and Weaving Mills Co. Ltd.

predicates.suit_against_statutory_body: The proceeding is a suit against a body established or empowered by statute.
predicates.claim_is_for_nonpayment_due_to_contract_: The claimant seeks payment allegedly due because the statutory body breached a contract.
predicates.nonpayment_not_reasonably_connected_to_s: The alleged non-payment has no reasonable connection with a duty imposed on the body or its agents by statute.

issues.definition: A suit against a statutory body for non-payment due to contract breach is not barred by a special limitation rule for statutory acts when the non-payment has no reasonable connection to a statutory duty.
